newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Stocks quiet after hours.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Stocks quiet after hours.

text.p: Traders said there was little after-hours activity Thursday as Wall Street eased toward the weekend.

Phillips-Van Heusen announced a restructuring, Ingram Micro Inc reported second quarter earnings of $0.27 a share, in-line with Wall Street estimates, and Federal Express reported a "dramatic" rise on volume from fears of a strike at United Parcel Service of America Inc.
None of the announcements spurred any after-close dealing, however.
"It's hot out. People want to go home," one trader said.
After rallying all week the Dow retreated a bit ahead Friday's employment report, closing at 8223.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one had volume of 8,400, compared with 2,100 Wednesday, and session two had volume of nearly 2.3 million, compared with 2.9 million.
